summary: This note is the source code for basiclogpy, a Python example from Bitcraze's Crazyflie Nano Quadcopter client (GPL-licensed, Copyright 2014 Bitcraze AB). It scans for the first Crazyflie found, connects to it, and configures a log of the Stabilizer roll, pitch and yaw variables at a 10 ms period, printing the data to the console. The example disconnects after a timer, with the docstring saying 5 seconds in the class and 10 seconds in the module header.
one_line: Python example that connects to the first Crazyflie quadcopter found and logs its Stabilizer roll, pitch and yaw to the console.
key_facts: basiclogpy is a Simple example from the Crazyflie Nano Quadcopter client, Copyright (C) 2014 Bitcraze AB, licensed under the GNU General Public License.
The example connects to the first Crazyflie found, logs the Stabilizer and prints it to the console.
The module docstring states that after 10s the application disconnects and exits.
The LoggingExample class docstring states that it disconnects after 5s.
The LogConfig is named 'Stabilizer' with period_in_ms=10.
The logged variables are stabilizer.roll, stabilizer.pitch and stabilizer.yaw, each of type 'float'.
The disconnect timer is created with Timer(5, self._cf.close_link).
logging.basicConfig is set to level=logging.ERROR so only errors from the logging framework are output.
In the connected callback, a KeyError from a missing TOC variable prints 'Could not start log configuration' and an AttributeError prints 'Could not add Stabilizer log config, bad configuration.'
The _stab_log_data callback prints the timestamp, logconf name and data for each received log packet.
The main block calls cflib.crtp.init_drivers(enable_debug_driver=False) and then cflib.crtp.scan_interfaces().
If no Crazyflies are found, the script prints 'No Crazyflies found, cannot run example'.
The main loop waits with time.sleep(1) while le.is_connected remains true.
